tasks.short: Collect rule updates and send a signed bulletin

steps.what: Record the source and document to watch
Collect new versions from the watch list
Draft a bulletin that quotes the source

loop.input: fetched text and its document id
loop.output: bulletin items that quote that text only
loop.check: Every quoted sentence appears in the fetched text and carries that document id
loop.stop: One draft; drop any sentence with no document id and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: A new legal text is not a fixed set of fields

steps.what: Sign which items staff must act on
Distribute the signed standards bulletin
Flag a product the bulletin affects

tasks.design: The specialist keeps a {WORKFLOW} watch list of source name, document id, market and product family. New versions land in {DOCS}. A bounded bulletin quotes only those texts, the specialist signs which items require action, and only that bulletin goes out by {EMAIL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Updates arrived as links and forwarded mail, so a bulletin could not show which document and which version it quoted.
tasks.enabler_now: A watch row can store a document id and a version date, and the fetched text can be kept next to that id.
tasks.still_hard: Whether a new text requires staff to act is a judgement, and the specialist confirms which rule it is.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides which items are action, which are information only, and what the bulletin is allowed to say.

ambition.what: Sign a bulletin in the week a watched document changes, not in a quarterly round-up

tasks.altitude: Collection is no longer the week. The specialist can withhold an item that has no document id, and staff see only the signed bulletin.

reach.task: Check a product against the signed bulletin
reach.learn: Which items were signed as action and which were filed as no change

evidence.claim: The digest's deterministic-first section groups letter-like drafts as a bounded loop over approved sources, with a named person signing.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly repaid a public report that cited sources that did not exist, so a bulletin must not invent a citation or an instrument number.
Which instrument applies is confirmed by the specialist for the market and the product. This task does not name one.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when the signed internal bulletin is sent. Filing a submission to an agency is a different task.

Input contract: source name, document id, version date, market, product family, fetched text. Producer of the watch row is the specialist. A source with no document id is not fetched. If the fetch returns no text, that item is omitted and listed as missing.
The prior treats the reach as external action. Here the external part is reading a public text. Distribution is an internal bulletin. Native mail and document templates are used before custom code.
unknowns: Which sources the firm is allowed to store a copy of.
Who receives a bulletin for each product family.
Who may sign when the specialist is absent.
research_questions: What share of watched documents change in a typical month?
What share of signed items are action rather than information only?

already_counted.description: Specialist deletes a quote that does not match the source
The action decision stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Retire watch rows when a source changes its document id
Quality reviewers clear flags that named the wrong product

approvals.approved_version: bulletin version signed for this watch period

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes most sources have no stable document id, so collection stays manual and the draft rarely quotes cleanly. The high case assumes the watch list is clean but every action decision and every signature stays with the specialist. Agency filings are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Draft the session from the signed procedure

loop.input: signed procedure version and any existing module id
loop.output: outline that cites that procedure version, or the module id
loop.check: The outline cites the signed procedure version, or it returns only an existing module id
loop.stop: If no procedure version is signed, return an empty outline and stop
loop.why_not_simpler: A new procedure has no module yet, and the wording has to follow that text

steps.what: Sign the training version to be taught
Deliver the regulatory training session
Attend the signed training session
Record completion for the signed session
Answer questions the outline did not cover

tasks.design: A bounded outline in {DOCS} is drafted from the signed procedure version, or it points at a module the {LMS} already has. The specialist signs the session and delivers it. The learning record stores completion only for that signed session. Questions outside the outline stay in the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: Slides were copied forward without a procedure version, so completion could not show what people were actually taught.
tasks.enabler_now: The learning system can store a session id tied to a procedure version, and completion can be written only for that id.
tasks.still_hard: Delivering the session and handling live questions stays with the specialist. People are not scored.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist decides what is taught, signs that version, and answers what the outline does not cover.

ambition.what: People who join between the yearly sessions can take the signed session without waiting for the annual day

tasks.altitude: Preparation shrinks to the outline and the signature. The specialist still stands in the room, and completion is not recorded for an unsigned session.

reach.task: Attend the session that matches the signed procedure
reach.learn: Which procedure version this session teaches and whether their completion was recorded

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm the session itself is the time. The outline is smaller, and a room full of questions does not become a record.
Digest [S23] says the Dutch works council must consent to HR data processing and to staff monitoring. A training completion record is HR data.

Digest [S22] says a data protection assessment is mandatory for employee monitoring, fraud prevention and credit scoring. Storing completion is not those three, and this design does not watch how people work.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task covers preparing and delivering the regulatory session. It does not grade people or decide employment consequences.

Input contract: procedure id, signed procedure version, session id, module id if one exists, audience role, date. Producer of the procedure version is the specialist's earlier signature. If no procedure version is signed, the outline is not drafted and the session is not recorded.

Configure the learning system's own course and completion fields before custom code. Works-council consent for the completion record is counted in access days, not assumed to be done. The design does not score learners and does not judge emotion or attention.
unknowns: Whether a works council has already consented to training completion records.
Which audiences must attend which procedure.
Who delivers the session when the specialist is absent.
research_questions: What share of sessions already have a learning module for that procedure version?
How often do questions fall outside the outline?

already_counted.description: Specialist edits an outline that drifts from the procedure
Delivery time in the room stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Retire an outline when the signed procedure version changes
Learners chase a completion that was recorded on the wrong session

approvals.approved_version: training session version signed for this procedure version
the same signed training session version

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes procedures have no signed version, so outlines stay hand-built and completion stays a manual list. The high case assumes the outline is clean but delivery, live questions and the signature stay manual. Attendance time of learners is not treated as specialist time saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write or update a standard operating procedure

steps.what: Submit the procedure change request
Draft the section from the signed source

loop.input: source passage, section id and the current section text
loop.output: replacement section that quotes the source
loop.check: The draft names the same section id and cites the source document id
loop.stop: One draft; leave the section blank if the source passage is missing
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot reorder a work instruction whose steps depend on that passage

steps.what: Try the draft instruction on one case
Sign the standard procedures version staff must follow
Publish only the signed procedure version

tasks.design: The quality reviewer submits procedure id, section id, reason and source document id on a {WORKFLOW} form. A bounded draft in {DOCS} rewrites that section only from the source passage. The specialist signs the version after a floor check, and only that version is published.
tasks.previous_blocker: Procedures were rewritten from memory, so a new section could not show the source passage it was supposed to follow.
tasks.enabler_now: The change request can carry a section id and a source document id, and the current section text can be opened beside it.
tasks.still_hard: A work instruction has to be followable on the floor, and a source passage does not by itself say the step order.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist accepts the wording and signs the version staff must follow. A failed floor check stops publication.

ambition.what: Update the procedure when the signed source changes, not only at the periodic rewrite

tasks.altitude: Drafting a section takes less of the week. The specialist still signs, and the register shows the signed version only after that signature.

reach.task: Run the work instruction once before it is published
reach.learn: Which section version is signed and which draft failed the floor check

evidence.claim: The digest's deterministic-first section groups procedure drafts as a bounded loop over approved sources, with a named person signing.
Digest [S27] says a consultancy partly repaid a public report that cited sources that did not exist, so a procedure section must not invent a source passage.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task ends when the signed procedure version is published and the previous version is retired. Training on it is a separate task.

Input contract: procedure id, section id, reason, source document id, source passage, current section text. Producer of the request is the quality reviewer. If the source passage is missing, the draft is blank and the specialist writes that section by hand or stops.
Use the document store's templates and version history before custom code. A material edit after the floor check is a new version and is not published on the old signature.
unknowns: Who on the floor is allowed to run the trial.
Whether retired versions must stay readable for audits.
Who may sign when the specialist is absent.
research_questions: What share of change requests arrive without a source passage?
How often does the floor check fail the first draft?

already_counted.description: Specialist rewrites a section the draft got wrong
Signature and last edits stay with the specialist

incremental.description: Adjust the section template when a new procedure type appears
Quality reviewers repeat a floor check after a material edit

approvals.approved_version: procedure version signed after this floor check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes requests lack a source passage, so the draft is blank and the specialist still writes the section. The high case assumes the source is attached but the floor check, the edits and the signature stay manual. Teaching the procedure is not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Define and track a quality metric

steps.what: Confirm the metric definition fields
Extract period counts for the quality metrics
Review exceptions and sign the snapshot
Publish only the signed metric snapshot
Repair a metric whose extract broke
Read the signed snapshot for the project

tasks.design: The quality reviewer confirms metric id, numerator, denominator, period and product family on a {WORKFLOW} form. A {BI} extract fills the period counts and replaces the {SPREADSHEET} once those fields exist. The specialist signs the snapshot, and only that snapshot is published.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counts lived in workbooks with different period labels, so a chart could not tell a real change from a broken extract.
tasks.enabler_now: The source can emit metric id, numerator, denominator and period as fields a view can filter.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing what the metric means, and whether a broken period is a real signal, stays with the specialist. No target number is invented here.
tasks.human_edge: The specialist signs the period snapshot and decides which exception is a fault in the extract rather than a result.

ambition.what: Sign the snapshot every period instead of rebuilding the workbook for the audit

tasks.altitude: The specialist stops pasting counts and keeps the exception list. An unsigned period is not shown as the firm's figure.

reach.task: Read the signed snapshot for the product
reach.learn: Which period is signed and which extract failed

evidence.claim: The digest's deterministic-first section treats reports, records and monitoring as a records app or a dashboard on operational data, not as a new judgement.
In a mid-size firm the metric workbook is rebuilt from exports. The definition and the exception call stay with a person.

assumptions: Focal role is the regulatory affairs specialist. The task is defining and tracking the metric. It does not set a pass threshold and it does not start a corrective project.

Input contract: metric id, numerator, denominator, period, product family, source record id. Producer of the definition is the quality reviewer. If the source has no metric id, the extract does not run and the specialist keeps the workbook for that metric.
Configure the existing report view before a custom extract. The meeting share in the prior does not fit this task: the time is the workbook and the exception list. This design does not score staff.
unknowns: Which source system holds the counts.
Whether a failed extract should hide the period or show it as missing.
Who may sign a snapshot when the specialist is absent.
research_questions: What share of metrics already have a stable metric id in the source?
How often is a signed snapshot later corrected?

already_counted.description: Exception review and the signature stay with the specialist
Repair of a broken extract stays with the specialist

incremental.description: Add a metric field when a new product family is tracked
Quality reviewers correct a definition the extract rejected

approvals.approved_version: metric snapshot signed for this period and metric id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the source has no metric id, so the extract does not run and the workbook remains. The high case assumes counts arrive clean but every snapshot is still signed and every broken period is still reviewed. No target or threshold is treated as saved work.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The specialist stops hunting for texts and rebuilding metric sheets, and keeps the week for signing bulletins, teaching the session and reading exceptions.
reach: Project leads receive the signed bulletin and the signed procedure version.
Quality reviewers receive the signed metric snapshot and the procedure that passed a floor check.
skills_to_grow: Tie a bulletin item to a source document id before anyone is asked to act.
Teach from a signed procedure version rather than from a slide with no source.
Define a metric as numerator, denominator and period before a chart is drawn.
role.ambitious_version: A rule change becomes one signed bulletin, one signed procedure version and a training session that uses that same version.
